browse_catalogue.description: List the values 'Find products' can filter by: brands, categories, labels, ingredients or countries, most-used first, each with how many products carry it. Use it to see what a filter can be set to, to find how the database spells something, or to answer a question of its own: which label claims are most common, how many products a brand has. Open Beauty Facts publishes the hundred most-used values of each, and the result says how many there are in total.

check_ingredients.description: Read a product's ingredient list and say which of the groups people commonly avoid are in it. It knows twelve: parabens, sulfates, silicones, fragrance and its declarable allergens, drying alcohol, formaldehyde releasers, isothiazolinone preservatives, PEGs, mineral oil, aluminium salts and chemical UV filters. Each one names the ingredient that put it there. Add your own ingredients to watch for as well. It also reports the groups that are not present, because 'no parabens' is usually the answer being looked for. This reports what the list contains; it is not a safety assessment, and the list is contributed by volunteers.

check_ingredients.name: check_ingredients

parameters.description: Which groups to look for. Leave all of them unticked to check every group.
parameters.name: avoid

options.label: Parabens: preservatives whose names end in -paraben
Sulfates: SLS, SLES and the other foaming detergents, not every ingredient with sulfate in its name
Silicones: dimethicone, siloxanes and the rest of the -cone family
Fragrance (parfum): an undeclared fragrance blend, however it is spelled
Declarable fragrance allergens: the 26 fragrance compounds EU labelling names separately, such as limonene and linalool
Drying alcohol: alcohol denat. and ethanol, not the fatty alcohols such as cetyl or stearyl alcohol
Formaldehyde releasers: preservatives that work by releasing formaldehyde slowly
Isothiazolinone preservatives: MI and MCI, common contact allergens in rinse-off products
PEGs and ethoxylates: PEG- and PPG- compounds, polysorbates and the -eth family
Mineral oil and petrolatum: petroleum-derived occlusives, including paraffinum liquidum
Aluminium salts: the antiperspirant salts, not aluminium used as a thickener or a colour
Chemical UV filters: the absorbing sunscreen filters, as opposed to zinc or titanium

parameters.description: Optional. Your own ingredients to watch for, separated by commas; a personal allergen, say. Part of a name is enough: nickel finds Nickel Sulfate.

compare_products.description: Put two to five products side by side by barcode and work out what they share and what only one of them has: which ingredients are in every one, which are in just this one, and the categories and label claims they have in common. The answer to 'which of these two should I buy' is the difference, not two lists printed one after the other. Ingredient lists are read off photographs of the pack, so the comparison uses the entries Open Beauty Facts recognised as ingredients; each product's full list comes back with it.

find_products.description: Search about 75,000 cosmetics by words, and narrow by category, brand, label, ingredient or the country a product is sold in. Use it to find a product's barcode from its name, to list every vegan deodorant, or to find what contains an ingredient. Each filter is a dropdown of values the database actually holds, so a filter that matches nothing is rare, and when it happens the result says so rather than coming back as an empty list.

get_product.description: Look a cosmetic up by the barcode on its pack and get everything Open Beauty Facts holds about it: the name and brand, the size, what kind of product it is, the claims on the label, the ingredient list as printed, how long it lasts after opening, where it is sold, and the photographs of the pack. A barcode nobody has entered yet, and a barcode that turns out to be a food or a pet food rather than a cosmetic, both come back as an answer saying which, rather than as an error, so a workflow can branch on it.

description: Look up cosmetics by barcode in Open Beauty Facts, the free, open database of about 75,000 shampoos, creams, deodorants, make-up and soaps built by volunteers. Read a product's ingredient list, brand, category, label claims, shelf life after opening and pack photographs; search or filter by category, brand, label, ingredient or country; check an ingredient list for the groups people commonly avoid; compare products side by side; and watch for products added since a date. No account and no API key. The data is contributed voluntarily and carries no guarantee of accuracy or completeness, so check it before relying on it for an allergy or a health decision.
